inlines.text: Meta 最新的应用
Forum，
面向所有想更深入参与其 Facebook 群组对话的人。
为了构建 Forum，Meta 的工程师采用了一种全新的工作方式，将 AI 智能体引入开发周期。
我们分享构建 Forum 过程中使用智能体式 AI 的洞察：我们如何调整代码库、为智能体执行测试框架和内部工具，哪些做法有效，哪些无效。

blocks.text: Forum 是一款独立的小组应用，由一个小团队从零开始构建。它也是我们测试一种不同工作方式的场所：将 AI 智能体视为工程流程的参与者，而不是更快的打字方式。

inlines.text: Forum 是一款独立的小组应用，由一个小团队从零开始构建。它也是我们测试一种不同工作方式的场所：将 AI 智能体视为工程流程的参与者，而不是更快的打字方式。

blocks.text: 这项实验需要定义成功，而我们的标准不是代码量。我们衡量的是经过验证、可投入生产的结果——能够构建、通过测试并经受审查的变更。

inlines.text: 这项实验需要定义成功，而我们的标准不是代码量。我们衡量的是经过验证、可投入生产的结果——能够构建、通过测试并经受审查的变更。

blocks.text: 从 Human-In-The-Loop 到 Human-On-The-Loop

inlines.text: 从 Human-In-The-Loop 到 Human-On-The-Loop

blocks.text: 仅将 AI 指向编码步骤本身并不会带来太大改变。当我们将这一方法扩展到实现前后的各个阶段——规划、构建、测试和验证——我们的成果开始复利式增长。看清这一转变最直观的方式，是看每个步骤由谁主导。

inlines.text: 仅将 AI 指向编码步骤本身并不会带来太大改变。当我们将这一方法扩展到实现前后的各个阶段——规划、构建、测试和验证——我们的成果开始复利式增长。看清这一转变最直观的方式，是看每个步骤由谁主导。

blocks.text: 在 human-in-the-loop 模式下，工程师驱动每一步，AI 在其中辅助，自动补全函数、建议修复方案或回答问题。每次迭代都以驱动者本人的节奏推进。

inlines.text: 在
human-in-the-loop
模式下，工程师驱动每一步，AI 在其中辅助，自动补全函数、建议修复方案或回答问题。每次迭代都以驱动者本人的节奏推进。

blocks.text: 在 human-on-the-loop 模式下，智能体自行运行迭代——规划、实现、构建、测试、修正、重复——而工程师设定目标、观察运行、在偏离时介入并批准结果。人的工作从执行步骤转变为对结果负责并守住质量标准。这是我们努力的方向，而非已完成的终态：如今有些阶段已能自主运行，而另一些阶段仍需工程师参与每次迭代。

human-on-the-loop
模式下，智能体自行运行迭代——规划、实现、构建、测试、修正、重复——而工程师设定目标、观察运行、在偏离时介入并批准结果。人的工作从执行步骤转变为对结果负责并守住质量标准。这是我们努力的方向，而非已完成的终态：如今有些阶段已能自主运行，而另一些阶段仍需工程师参与每次迭代。

blocks.text: 当工程师进行监督时，工作不再是严格的顺序执行。过去一次只能运行一个的循环可以重叠，工程师的时间用于方向和判断，而不是坐在循环里等待。但这一切只有在返回的结果可信时才成立。没有验证，AI 生成的代码会带来一个熟悉的问题——看似合理但无人确认其真正可用的输出，工程师随后不得不阅读、调试，并常常将其丢弃。弱信号并不能消除这一约束；它们只是把约束从编写代码转移到审查那些看起来已完成、实则不然的代码上。

inlines.text: 当工程师进行监督时，工作不再是严格的顺序执行。过去一次只能运行一个的循环可以重叠，工程师的时间用于方向和判断，而不是坐在循环里等待。但这一切只有在返回的结果可信时才成立。没有验证，AI 生成的代码会带来一个熟悉的问题——看似合理但无人确认其真正可用的输出，工程师随后不得不阅读、调试，并常常将其丢弃。弱信号并不能消除这一约束；它们只是把约束从编写代码转移到审查那些看起来已完成、实则不然的代码上。

blocks.text: 因此我们把标准设在验证而非编译上。编译不是终点——只有自动化测试和视觉检查都通过，任务才算完成。智能体在工程师看到之前先检查自己的工作，这意味着到达审查环节的是一组数量更少、可信度更高的结果，而不是一堆需要筛选的输出。生成得更少，丢弃的也更少。每个交付的结果仍需工程师签字确认；我们的努力在于让这一签字确认快速且有据可依，将构建结果、测试结果和录制的验证会话附加到变更上。

blocks.text: 当工程师置身于每个循环之外时，循环必须能安全地自行运行。四项能力使之成为可能：

blocks.text: 将规划作为技术规范： 智能体执行需要极高的精确度。工程师可能凭直觉解决的歧义会导致智能体失败。我们投入于严格的上游分解和机器可读的上下文，这为工程师和智能体同样收紧了工程闭环。

inlines.text: 将规划作为技术规范：
智能体执行需要极高的精确度。工程师可能凭直觉解决的歧义会导致智能体失败。我们投入于严格的上游分解和机器可读的上下文，这为工程师和智能体同样收紧了工程闭环。

blocks.text: 循环内的自动化验证是力量倍增器： 我们将自动化的通过/失败信号——构建状态、单元测试和 UI 规范匹配——直接集成到智能体循环中。这使得异步开发能够产出可供审查的拉取请求，并预先填充测试计划和录制的验证会话。验证是最难做对的部分，而我们能安全地交给循环多少，取决于我们能多大程度信任验证器。

blocks.text: 使用智能体进行模拟用户测试： 我们部署了导航智能体，它们像真人一样与实时应用交互。这些智能体执行操作、读取屏幕并报告回归问题。导航智能体能够持续运行相同的验证路径。

blocks.text: 智能体化生产运维：发布后，智能体帮助自动化根因分析。当使用 Forum 的人提交反馈时，智能体会利用该反馈调查可能的回归问题。随后智能体将分析转发给工程师，由工程师决定下一步行动。

blocks.text: 运营模式

inlines.text: 运营模式

blocks.text: 这种所有权模式需要具备五个关键组件的机制：

inlines.text: 这种所有权模式需要具备五个关键组件的机制：
规则
是永久性的项目指令。当智能体重复犯错超过两次时，我们将纠正措施一次性编码，供所有人使用。
技能
将团队约定转化为智能体可以调用的可加载步骤。
智能体
自动化此前需要人工通过的检查。
命令
将技能和智能体串联成工作流。它们评估复杂度、复现缺陷、规划并实施修复、创建拉取请求，并运行多阶段审查。
钩子
是自动化触发器，例如在每次智能体回合后运行 linter、在安装前检查模拟器连接性，以及在创建拉取请求前验证测试。

blocks.text: 让环境适应模型

inlines.text: 让环境适应模型

blocks.text: 最大的收益来自改变我们的代码和工具，而非提示词。

inlines.text: 最大的收益来自改变我们的代码和工具，而非提示词。

blocks.text: 架构清晰性优先于继承的复杂性： 我们努力保持 Forum 的代码库尽可能简单直接，并选择将架构的关键部分模块化，以便在获得久经考验的基础设施优势的同时，也让智能体能够轻松即插即用。在无法轻易做到的地方，我们从头重建，以复用性换取智能体吞吐量，事实证明这在开发速度上很有回报。智能体从它们阅读的代码中学习模式。修复一次薄弱的模式，未来每个智能体会话都会继承这一改进；放任不管，同样的捷径就会出现在智能体接下来编写的所有内容中。

inlines.text: 架构清晰性优先于继承的复杂性：
我们努力保持 Forum 的代码库尽可能简单直接，并选择将架构的关键部分模块化，以便在获得久经考验的基础设施优势的同时，也让智能体能够轻松即插即用。在无法轻易做到的地方，我们从头重建，以复用性换取智能体吞吐量，事实证明这在开发速度上很有回报。智能体从它们阅读的代码中学习模式。修复一次薄弱的模式，未来每个智能体会话都会继承这一改进；放任不管，同样的捷径就会出现在智能体接下来编写的所有内容中。

blocks.text: 给智能体工具，而不是描述：我们的主要失败模式是智能体搞不清自己在应用中的位置——让它修改群组主页时却去编辑首页信息流，或者靠猜屏幕坐标。所以，我们没有向智能体描述应用，而是给它工具去核查：从模拟器读取实时视图层级、列出屏幕上实际存在的元素、查找通往目标视图的路径——全部在它行动之前完成。误操作的编辑大幅减少。我们在智能体接触系统的所有地方都采用了同样的方法：给智能体一种直接核查状态的方式，而不是让它基于描述去推理。

我们的主要失败模式是智能体搞不清自己在应用中的位置——让它修改群组主页时却去编辑首页信息流，或者靠猜屏幕坐标。所以，我们没有向智能体描述应用，而是给它工具去核查：从模拟器读取实时视图层级、列出屏幕上实际存在的元素、查找通往目标视图的路径——全部在它行动之前完成。误操作的编辑大幅减少。我们在智能体接触系统的所有地方都采用了同样的方法：给智能体一种直接核查状态的方式，而不是让它基于描述去推理。

blocks.text: 为安全的 AI 原型开发提供构建级隔离：随着 Forum 逐步走向生产环境，我们希望早期原型和智能体生成的实验有运行空间，同时让生产应用严格只包含已完成、经过审查的工作。我们想要比单纯的功能开关更强的保证——功能开关下原型代码仍然存在于生产构建中。我们的解决方案是一个独立的构建变体，一个沙盒应用，它与生产环境共享完全相同的代码库、框架和设计系统，但通过插件/套接字架构将原型代码完全排除在生产构建之外。

blocks.text: 这让我们同时获得了三样东西：

inlines.text: 这让我们同时获得了三样东西：
设计师和跨职能伙伴可以自由使用 AI 工具做原型，无需每个改动都让工程师参与。
在沙盒中构建的任何东西都可以直接移植到生产环境，无需重新构建。
任何原型代码都不会让生产应用崩溃，因为它在那个构建中根本不存在。

blocks.text: 用 AI 压力测试发现真实缺陷

inlines.text: 用 AI 压力测试发现真实缺陷

blocks.text: 改造环境不仅让智能体构建起来更快——它还让智能体成了测试员。我们没有把它指向某个具体缺陷。相反，我们设置了可重复的压力场景来模拟真实用户行为（激进滚动、随机浏览群组、快速导航、反复加载媒体），并在各构建中例行运行。由于这些运行会产生一致的信号（崩溃、内存增长、页面错误、UI 回归），智能体可以分诊异常、缩小到触发序列，然后调查根本原因。

inlines.text: 改造环境不仅让智能体构建起来更快——它还让智能体成了测试员。我们没有把它指向某个具体缺陷。相反，我们设置了可重复的压力场景来模拟真实用户行为（激进滚动、随机浏览群组、快速导航、反复加载媒体），并在各构建中例行运行。由于这些运行会产生一致的信号（崩溃、内存增长、页面错误、UI 回归），智能体可以分诊异常、缩小到触发序列，然后调查根本原因。

blocks.text: 其中一次运行暴露了一个内存问题。智能体隔离出复现步骤、提出修复方案并验证了它——全部在开发期间完成，早于应用到达用户手中。该修复在反复的压力会话中显著减少了设备上的内存增长和页面错误。

blocks.text: 虽然架构决策由工程师做出，但检测和回归监控是自动化且可重复的；一旦检测到异常，智能体就能用同一套测试框架完成复现 → 隔离 → 提出修复 → 验证。

blocks.text: 它奏效了吗？

blocks.text: 文章 How Meta Built Forum With AI-Native Engineering 首次发表于 Engineering at Meta。

inlines.text: 文章
How Meta Built Forum With AI-Native Engineering
首次发表于
Engineering at Meta
Meta’s newest app,
Forum,
is for anyone who wants to go deeper into the conversations in their Facebook groups.
To build Forum, Meta engineers adopted a whole new way of working by bringing an AI agent into the development cycle.
We’re sharing insights into what it took to build Forum with agentic AI: how we adapted the codebase, tested frameworks and internal tooling for agentic execution, what worked, and what didn’t.

blocks.text: Forum is a standalone Groups app that a small team built from scratch. It’s also where we tested a different way of working: treating an AI agent as a participant in the engineering process rather than a faster way to type.

inlines.text: Forum is a standalone Groups app that a small team built from scratch. It’s also where we tested a different way of working: treating an AI agent as a participant in the engineering process rather than a faster way to type.

blocks.text: That experiment needed a definition of success, and ours wasn’t code volume. We measured verified, production-ready outcomes — changes that build, pass tests, and survive review.

inlines.text: That experiment needed a definition of success, and ours wasn’t code volume. We measured verified, production-ready outcomes — changes that build, pass tests, and survive review.

blocks.text: From Human-In-The-Loop to Human-On-The-Loop

inlines.text: From Human-In-The-Loop to Human-On-The-Loop

blocks.text: Pointing AI at the coding step alone doesn’t change much. Our results compounded as we extended the approach to the stages around implementation — planning, building, testing, and verification. The clearest way to see the shift is in who owns each step.

inlines.text: Pointing AI at the coding step alone doesn’t change much. Our results compounded as we extended the approach to the stages around implementation — planning, building, testing, and verification. The clearest way to see the shift is in who owns each step.

blocks.text: With human-in-the-loop, the engineer drives every step and the AI assists inside it by autocompleting a function, suggesting a fix, or answering a question. Each iteration advances at the pace of the person driving it.

inlines.text: With
human-in-the-loop
, the engineer drives every step and the AI assists inside it by autocompleting a function, suggesting a fix, or answering a question. Each iteration advances at the pace of the person driving it.

blocks.text: With human-on-the-loop, the agent runs the iteration itself — plan, implement, build, test, correct, repeat — while the engineer sets the goal, watches the run, steps in when it drifts, and approves the result. The person’s job moves from executing the steps to owning the outcome and holding the quality bar. This is the target we are driving toward, not a finished state: some stages run autonomously today, while others still keep an engineer in each iteration.

human-on-the-loop

, the agent runs the iteration itself — plan, implement, build, test, correct, repeat — while the engineer sets the goal, watches the run, steps in when it drifts, and approves the result. The person’s job moves from executing the steps to owning the outcome and holding the quality bar. This is the target we are driving toward, not a finished state: some stages run autonomously today, while others still keep an engineer in each iteration.

blocks.text: When the engineer supervises, work stops being strictly sequential. Cycles that used to run one at a time can overlap, and an engineer’s time goes to direction and judgment rather than to sitting through the loop. But that only holds if what comes back can be trusted. Without verification, AI-generated code creates a familiar problem — plausible output that no one has confirmed actually works, which an engineer then has to read, debug, and often discard. Weak signals don’t remove the constraint; they move it from writing code to reviewing code that looks finished and isn’t.

But that only holds if what comes back can be trusted. Without verification, AI-generated code creates a familiar problem — plausible output that no one has confirmed actually works, which an engineer then has to read, debug, and often discard. Weak signals don’t remove the constraint; they move it from writing code to reviewing code that looks finished and isn’t.

blocks.text: So we set the bar at verification rather than compilation. Compiling isn’t the finish line — a task is complete only once automated tests and visual checks have passed. Agents check their own work before an engineer sees it, which means what reaches review is a smaller set of higher-confidence results rather than a pile of output to sift through. Less gets generated, and less gets discarded. Every shipped outcome still carries an engineer’s sign-off; our effort went into making that sign-off fast and well-evidenced, with build results, test outcomes, and recorded verification sessions attached to the change.

blocks.text: With the engineer outside of every cycle, the loop has to run safely on its own. Four capabilities make that possible:

inlines.text: With the engineer outside of every cycle, the loop has to run safely on its own. Four capabilities make that possible:

blocks.text: Planning as technical specification: Agentic execution requires extreme precision. Ambiguity that an engineer might resolve through intuition results in agent failure. We invested in rigorous upstream decomposition and machine-readable context, which tightened the engineering loop for engineers and agents alike.

inlines.text: Planning as technical specification:

Agentic execution requires extreme precision. Ambiguity that an engineer might resolve through intuition results in agent failure. We invested in rigorous upstream decomposition and machine-readable context, which tightened the engineering loop for engineers and agents alike.

blocks.text: Automated verification inside the loop is the force multiplier: We integrated automated pass/fail signals — build status, unit tests, and UI spec matching — directly into the agent loop. This enabled asynchronous development producing ready-to-review pull requests with pre-populated test plans and recorded verification sessions. Verification is the hard part to get right, and how much we can safely hand to the loop is gated by how much we can trust the verifiers.

blocks.text: Simulated user testing with agents: We deployed navigation agents that interact with the live app exactly like a person would. These agents perform actions, read the screen, and report regressions. Navigation agents are able to run the same verification paths continuously.

blocks.text: Agentic production operations: After launch, agents help automate root-cause analysis. When someone using Forum submits feedback, the agents use that feedback to investigate possible regressions. The agents then forward the analysis to engineers who decide the next course of action.

blocks.text: The Operating Model

inlines.text: The Operating Model

blocks.text: That ownership model needs machinery with five key components:

inlines.text: That ownership model needs machinery with five key components:
Rules
are permanent project instructions. When the agent repeats a mistake more than twice, we encode the correction once, for everyone.
Skills
turn team conventions into loadable steps the agent can invoke.
Agents
automate checks that previously required a manual pass.
Commands
chain skills and agents into workflows. They assess complexity, reproduce a bug, plan and implement a fix, create the pull request, and run a multi-stage review.
Hooks
are automated triggers, such as running a linter after every agent turn, checking simulator connectivity before install, and validating tests before a pull request is created.

blocks.text: Adapting the Environment to the Models

inlines.text: Adapting the Environment to the Models

blocks.text: The biggest gains came from changing our code and tooling, not our prompts.

inlines.text: The biggest gains came from changing our code and tooling, not our prompts.

blocks.text: Architectural legibility over inherited complexity: We worked to keep Forum’s codebase as straightforward as possible and chose to modularize key pieces of the architecture in order to get the benefits of battle-tested infrastructure while also letting the agents plug and play easily. Where we couldn’t easily do so, we rebuilt from scratch, trading reuse for agentic throughput, and it proved rewarding in development speed. Agents learn patterns from the code they read. Fix a weak pattern once and every future agent session inherits the improvement; leave it and the same shortcut shows up in everything the agent writes next.

inlines.text: Architectural legibility over inherited complexity:

We worked to keep Forum’s codebase as straightforward as possible and chose to modularize key pieces of the architecture in order to get the benefits of battle-tested infrastructure while also letting the agents plug and play easily. Where we couldn’t easily do so, we rebuilt from scratch, trading reuse for agentic throughput, and it proved rewarding in development speed. Agents learn patterns from the code they read. Fix a weak pattern once and every future agent session inherits the improvement; leave it and the same shortcut shows up in everything the agent writes next.

blocks.text: Give agents tools, not descriptions: Our main failure mode was the agent losing track of where it was in the app — editing the home feed when asked to change the group home screen, or guessing at screen coordinates. So instead of describing the app to the agent, we gave it tools to check: read the live view hierarchy from the simulator, list the elements actually on screen, and look up the path to a target view — all before it acts. Misdirected edits dropped sharply. We applied the same approach wherever agents touched our systems: give the agent a way to check state directly rather than a description to reason from.

blocks.text: Build-level isolation for safe AI prototyping: As Forum matured toward production, we wanted early-stage prototypes and agent-generated experiments to have room to run while keeping the production app strictly limited to finished, reviewed work. We wanted a stronger guarantee than feature gating alone, where prototype code still exists inside the production build. Our solution was a separate build flavor, a sandbox app that shares the exact same codebase, frameworks, and design system as production, but compiles prototype code out of the production build entirely via a plugin/socket architecture.

blocks.text: This gave us three things at once:

inlines.text: This gave us three things at once:
Designers and cross-functional partners could prototype freely using AI tools without needing an engineer in the loop for each change.
Anything built in the sandbox could be ported directly to production with no rebuild.
No prototype code could crash the production app because it physically didn’t exist in that build.

blocks.text: The pattern let us keep fast AI iteration after we had real people using the app to protect.

blocks.text: Finding Real Bugs With AI Stress Testing

inlines.text: Finding Real Bugs With AI Stress Testing

blocks.text: Adapting the environment did more than make the agent faster to build with — it made the agent a tester. We didn’t point it at one specific defect. Instead, we set up repeatable stress scenarios that mimic real user behavior (aggressive scrolling, random group browsing, rapid navigation, repeated media loading) and ran them routinely across builds. Because these runs produce consistent signals (crashes, memory growth, page faults, UI regressions), the agent can triage anomalies, narrow to the triggering sequence, and then investigate the root cause.

inlines.text: Adapting the environment did more than make the agent faster to build with — it made the agent a tester. We didn’t point it at one specific defect. Instead, we set up repeatable stress scenarios that mimic real user behavior (aggressive scrolling, random group browsing, rapid navigation, repeated media loading) and ran them routinely across builds. Because these runs produce consistent signals (crashes, memory growth, page faults, UI regressions), the agent can triage anomalies, narrow to the triggering sequence, and then investigate the root cause.

blocks.text: One such run surfaced a memory issue. The agent isolated a repro, proposed a fix, and verified it — all during development, before the app reached users. The fix materially reduced on-device memory growth and page faults across repeated stress sessions.

blocks.text: Building the stack: Agents mapped the architectural options and trade-offs; engineers then evaluated and chose. What we deliberately kept human was the target — deciding what a good outcome looks like is a product judgment, not something the system should define for itself.

inlines.text: Building the stack:

Agents mapped the architectural options and trade-offs; engineers then evaluated and chose. What we deliberately kept human was the target — deciding what a good outcome looks like is a product judgment, not something the system should define for itself.

blocks.text: Operating the stack: Questions that used to require whichever engineer knew the relevant code path now go to an investigation agent that gathers what it needs and posts a write-up with suggested fixes. After hand-scoring a batch of real investigations we arrived at a workflow where the agent compresses the mechanical work and delivers a structured write-up to an engineer, who then validates whether a finding is a real bug or an intentional trade-off.

blocks.text: What improved quality wasn’t better prompting. It was context. One recurring category of investigation came back weak until we gave the agent the same pointers to the relevant code, example queries, and design docs that we’d give any new engineer on day one. The quality of that category jumped. The difference from human onboarding is that you train once, and every future session starts from it.

blocks.text: Did It Work?

inlines.text: Did It Work?

blocks.text: Beyond shipping faster, we shipped cleaner. Continuous verification surfaced systemic issues — like the memory bottleneck above — during development rather than after launch. The results show up in the performance profile:

inlines.text: Beyond shipping faster, we shipped cleaner. Continuous verification surfaced systemic issues — like the memory bottleneck above — during development rather than after launch. The results show up in the performance profile:
Quality, found early:
The autonomous stress-testing loop caught and fixed the aforementioned memory issue during development rather than post-launch, roughly halving memory use and page faults.
Velocity:
Forum reached core feature parity with Facebook Groups in eight weeks, with AI handling much of the routine implementation so engineers could focus on architecture, product decisions, and quality.
Leverage that lasted:
After launch, agent-driven investigation helped engineers triage and root-cause user feedback.

blocks.text: The AI did more than generate code. It tightened our quality loop, helping a small team deliver a high-quality app with less ongoing rework.
